Entities / Shattered Sea

The Shattered Sea

Overview

The Shattered Sea is a warm archipelago of roughly sixty thousand square miles: reef, deep channel, cliff port, free harbour, old ruin, colonial ledger, storm belt, and routes that punish anyone who mistakes a chart for the truth.

Two island arcs curve east to west across a wide channel of open water called the Central Strait. The northern arc is the Crown Islands — five large, fortified, Dravosi Crown-held islands where authority has faces and ledgers. The southern arc is the Midchain — dozens of low limestone and coral islands, free ports, reef channels, and water that can feed a careful crew and swallow a careless one.

Between them: the Strait, the trade route, the inspection chokepoint. West of the western entrance: the Galewall, the permanent storm belt and the only route to the colonial homelands. East of the eastern exit: the Outer Reach and the Drowned Maw — the planar trench, the last frontier, the place that ends expeditions.

Nobody owns the Shattered Sea. The Dravosi Crown claims the northern arc. The Tessarine Concordat controls the money. Umberlee controls the water tribute. Pilots, free ports, smugglers, and local bosses control the rest. Authority here is local, layered, and negotiated at each port.

Power & Governance

Dravosi Crown: Controls the northern arc and the Strait inspection regime. Fleet, forts, harbourmasters, ledgers.

Tessarine Concordat: Controls the credit, insurance, and trade underwriting. No forts — just obligation.

Umberlee and the Waveservants: Water tribute is practical infrastructure. Waveservants collect at every harbour. Skipping tribute is a choice captains make once.

Local power: Every free port has its own council, boss, or factor. Authority in the Midchain is neighbourhood by neighbourhood.

Navigation

The Scatter Current runs east through the Central Strait and turns north at the eastern end. Eastbound ships get half a knot for free. Westbound ships earn every mile. Pilots earn their fee because every chart in the Scatter has been wrong at least once — reef lines shift, new shoals appear, and the Drowned Maw’s compass drift increases the further east you go.
